newsitem.title: SLOVAKIA: Slovak FinMin says import moves reaction to Czechs.
newsitem.headline: Slovak FinMin says import moves reaction to Czechs.

text.p: Slovak Finance Minister Sergej Kozlik said on Wednesday a new government measure to impose import deposits for selected goods was a direct reaction to similar plans approved last week by the Czech government.

"We are not happy to have to impose such a measure but we have to react to changes in external conditions, mainly the Czech restriction of imports through import deposits," Kozlik told a news conference.

With effect from this Monday, the Czech government imposed a requirement on all importers of consumer and agricultural goods to place a sum equal to 20 percent of the value of the imports in non-interest bearing accounts in Czech banks for 180 days.
On Wednesday, Kozlik announced similar restrictions although he did not specify which goods will be affected.
The Czech Republic is Slovakia's largest trading partner, accounting for around 30 percent of overall Slovak exports.

Economic Minister Karol Cesnek told the same news conference that the Czech plan will seriously hurt Slovak exporters, since the Czech deposit measure will affect about 44 percent of Slovak exports to the Czech Republic.
Kozlik also said a law against subsidised imports should be ready for parliamentary discussion by May 31.
"The measures also call for the economic ministry to speed up the process of drafting laws for protection against excessive and subsidised imports."

The government on Tuesday approved quotas on imports of Czech soft drinks of 450,000 hectolitres a year. But Kozlik said this measure had been discussed with the Czech side within the framework of the customs union since the beginning of this year.

"The government also agreed to keep the lid on real wage increases as we are aware of slower growth of labour productivity compared to wages which occured last year and which can be dangerous to the economy," Kozlik said without further elaboration.
The government also plans to speed up preparation of a new bankruptcy law to allow quicker bankruptcy procedures.
